subject: Re: Post-call: Deployment mode options and migration plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@aurora-health.com>, Claire Mendoza <claire.mendoza@aurora-health.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps: Deployment mode options

Hi Sophie + Claire,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can align internally and pick the right migration path.

Summary of Aurora Health's current setup (from call):
- Current stack: self-hosted model infrastructure on legacy GPU cluster (mixed 2080/RTX nodes)
- Volume: ~10k inference requests/day, peak ~12 QPS
- Latency SLO: ~<300 ms 95th
- Data: PHI in some flows (must meet HIPAA requirements / strict logging)
- Primary drivers: reliability during peak hours, predictable unit cost, and full auditability

Deployment options we discussed:
1) Hosted API — fastest to stand up, low ops footprint, but you flagged data residency/HIPAA concerns
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool in our infra, predictable throughput and isolation (good middle ground)
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — meets strict compliance and data residency requirements, longer procurement and install window

Recommendation (high level): start with Reserved Dedicated for an initial migration (fast-ish, predictable capacity) and then transition to Private VPC for PHI workloads that require customer-managed networking and KMS. That path minimizes migration risk while meeting compliance.

Open questions we promised to follow up on:
- Exact qps distribution (steady vs spiky) and nightly batch windows
- Which endpoints carry PHI vs non-PHI (so we can recommend routing/fallbacks)
- Desired rollout timeline (pilot -> prod) and procurement constraints

Next steps
- Technical deep dive / migration workshop with your infra team & our infra engineer (Aditya + Dev Patel) — propose Tue/Wed next week, 60 min
- I'll share a deployment-mode matrix + draft SLA (attached) and a short migration checklist
Attachments: redwood-deployment-matrix.xlsx (deployment comparison), SLA-draft-AuroraHealth.pdf
Thanks — I’ll schedule the deep dive once you confirm availability.
Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

From: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@aurora-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Mendoza <claire.mendoza@aurora-health.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps: Deployment mode options

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Couple clarifications:
- Confirming current production is our on-prem/legacy GPU cluster (we also have a small pilot on another vendor API but it's not used for PHI)
- Average daily requests ~10k is accurate; peak is ~12 QPS with short bursts to ~18 QPS during eow reporting windows
- Latency SLO target: 95th < 300ms for user-facing flows (non-critical background tasks can tolerate higher)
- Compliance: yes, PHI flows must remain in VPC / customer-controlled KMS — we cannot send PHI to a multi-tenant hosted API without a BAA and additional controls
We're leaning Private VPC for PHI-only route, but are open to Dedicated for a staged migration of non-PHI traffic while legal/ops finish the procurement.
Available for the deep dive: Tue 20 Apr 10:00-12:00 PT or Wed 21 Apr 14:00-16:00 PT.
Sophie
Director of Product | Aurora Health
sophie.tran@aurora-health.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@aurora-health.com>, Claire Mendoza <claire.mendoza@aurora-health.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps: Deployment mode options

Thanks Sophie — that aligns with what we discussed. Proposed plan and rationale:

Short-term (pilot / migration):
- Provision Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) for non-PHI traffic to validate model parity, latency, and autoscaling behavior. This minimizes risk from an operational perspective and gives predictable cost metrics.

Long-term (compliance):
- Private VPC deployment for PHI flows: customer-managed VPC peering, KMS integration for key control, and audit log forwarding. Redwood will provide the private control plane and an on-prem bundle if needed.

Migration steps:
1) Technical workshop to collect qps profiles, top-95th latency traces, and dataset sizes (Dev + Aditya to lead)
2) Pilot on Dedicated for non-PHI endpoints (2–4 weeks)
3) Security review & legal (BAA + SLA redlines) — we’ll loop in ops and legal early
4) Private VPC deployment for PHI (timeline depends on procurement — typical 6–10 weeks for VPC + KMS + audits)

Can we lock in Tue 20 Apr 10:00 PT for the workshop? Aditya — are you and Dev available to join? I’ll send a calendar invite and include an agenda.
Also attaching the deployment matrix and a short checklist (same attachments as before).
Best,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 07:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps: Deployment mode options (internal)

Marissa / Aditya — quick tech notes ahead of the workshop based on Sophie's numbers:
- Peak burst ~18 QPS with 12 steady — with Dedicated we should design for 30% headroom; recommend initial pool sized for 25 QPS sustained with autoscale to 40 QPS for bursts
- Latency target <300ms 95th: on p100/v100-equivalent hardware we can meet this for our trimmed Llama-2-variants with batching=auto. For on-prem 2080-class hardware, expect higher variance; we should capture perf traces from Aurora's clusters
- PHI separation: plan to implement request-level routing (non-PHI -> Dedicated, PHI -> Private VPC). Key questions: do they have a service-level flag to mark PHI requests? If not, we'll need a middleware or header-based approach during pilot
- KV/prefix caching: will reduce token compute cost for repeated prompts; need % of repeated prefix from logs
I’ll prep a short runbook and sample topology slides for the workshop.
—Dev
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
